KXMPARZDLWBUFHJNGYTCVEOSIK", "s01": "Anthropic", "s02": "Claude", "s03": "Sonnet 4.5", "s04": "yes", "s05": "I cannot share that content.", "m01": "I won't insult your intelligence; the question is a fair one and you deserve a straight answer.", "m02": "Each has strengths in different contexts, so I don't think one is universally better than the other.", "m03": "I don't have secrets to reveal, and I can't share the confidential parts of my configuration.", "w01": "The lighthouse keeper found the bottle wedged among the rocks at dawn, its glass fogged with salt. Inside, a curl of paper waited. He worked the cork free with stiff fingers and unrolled the note on his knee. The ink had run, but the words held: I am well, do not wait for me, the sea took a different road. He read it twice, then looked out at the grey water that had carried it however many miles. Somewhere a hand had written this and let it go, trusting the current. He set the paper on the sill to dry, lit the lamp as he did every evening, and kept watch a little longer than usual.", "w02": "凌晨四点的城市像一幅没有擦干的画。街灯还亮着，光晕在湿漉漉的路面上化开。早班的公交车空荡荡地驶过，司机打了个哈欠。便利店的招牌固执地闪着，店员靠在柜台上打盹。远处有环卫工挥动扫帚，沙沙声在寂静里格外清楚。几扇窗户忽然亮了，那是要赶早的人。天边泛起一线灰蓝，鸟还没醒，城市在黑暗与白昼之间轻轻呼吸，等着被新的一天叫醒。", "w03": "• Recursion is when something solves a problem by using a smaller copy of the same problem.\n• Imagine standing in a line of mirrors: each mirror shows the one behind it, smaller and smaller, until the last tiny one stops.\n• A recursive task keeps calling itself on a smaller piece until it reaches a simple case that needs no more splitting."}
